subject: Cloud Computing
title: Azure's 2023 Entra ID Outage
description: A micro-lesson that makes Azure's 2023 Entra ID Outage usable.

hook.text: In July 2023, Azure's identity service failed. Nobody could log in. No login means no access to anything.

buildup.text: Entra ID (formerly Azure AD) handles authentication for Microsoft 365, Teams, and thousands of enterprise apps.

discovery.text: A code change in authentication introduced a bug. It wasn't caught in testing because it only appeared at scale.

twist.text: Companies with no backup identity provider were completely locked out. SSO became a single point of total failure.

climax.text: The outage proved that identity services are the most critical cloud dependency. If auth fails, everything stops.

punchline.text: No login, no work. Identity is the most critical service.

quiz.question: Why was the Azure Entra ID outage so impactful?
options: Identity services control authentication — no login means no access to anything
Azure's data centers were physically damaged
The outage only affected test environments, not production

details.summary: In 2023, an Azure Entra ID outage disrupted authentication for Microsoft 365 and Azure services worldwide. Users could not sign in for hours, demonstrating how centralized identity services become critical single points of failure in cloud environments.
details.whyItMatters: Identity is the backbone of cloud access. When the authentication service goes down, every service behind it becomes inaccessible regardless of its individual health.
takeaways: Identity service failures lock users out of all connected services
Centralized authentication creates a single point of failure
Break-glass accounts and cached sessions mitigate impact

faq.question: Why are identity outages so impactful?
faq.answer: Every cloud service depends on authentication. When the identity provider fails, users cannot access any connected application, even perfectly healthy ones. The blast radius of an identity outage spans every service and user in the organization.

faq.question: How can organizations prepare for identity outages?
faq.answer: Configure break-glass emergency accounts with separate credentials, extend session token lifetimes for critical applications, implement cached authentication that works during brief outages, and document manual procedures for essential operations.
